title: Jest Quiz
description: Revisit the key ideas in Jest. Read each choice carefully. You can try the quiz again after reviewing the lessons.

questions.question: Which matcher compares this number?
questions.explanation: Jest runs a test function and reports whether its checks pass. expect gives the actual value; a matcher states the expected result. This test passes because 2 + 3 equals 5.

questions.question: Which matcher checks object contents?
questions.explanation: toEqual checks values inside objects. This is different from checking whether two names refer to the exact same object. The test passes because the title values match.

questions.question: What does toContain check?
questions.explanation: A length check and a containment check answer different questions about a list. Both checks pass: there are two books, and Moon is one of them.

questions.question: What should expect receive here?
questions.explanation: Pass a function to toThrow so Jest can call it and catch the error. The test passes when the function throws an error with the expected message.

questions.question: When does beforeEach run?
questions.explanation: beforeEach runs before each test in its scope. Use it to prepare fresh mutable data. The basket starts empty for the test. Another test can change its own fresh basket.

questions.question: What does jest.fn record?
questions.explanation: jest.fn makes a function that records calls. A mock can stand in for a small dependency. The test passes because save was called with 8. No real storage is needed.

questions.question: Which method sets a normal mock return value?
questions.explanation: A mock can return a chosen value so the code under test has predictable input. The mock returns Asha every time in this example.

questions.question: What does resolves inspect?
questions.explanation: An async test can await a promise. resolves checks the value with which it finishes successfully. The test waits and then passes because the resolved value is 8.

questions.question: Which matcher branch checks rejection?
questions.explanation: rejects checks a promise that fails. It is useful for an expected error path. The rejected promise is expected, so this test passes.

questions.question: How many test cases are listed?
questions.explanation: test.each runs a test with each row of data. A row contains inputs and expected output. Jest runs three cases for the doubling rule.

questions.question: Why restore real timers?
questions.explanation: Fake timers let a test move time forward without really waiting. Restore real timers when the test ends. The reminder runs once when fake time advances by 1000 milliseconds.

questions.question: What should you do before updating a snapshot?
questions.explanation: A snapshot stores an expected structure. Review changes instead of accepting a new snapshot blindly. The test checks a small saved object shape. A changed title should cause a review.
